subject: Advanced Microeconomics
text: A firm faces the market demand function P=100-2Q and has a total cost function TC=20Q. Construct the equilibrium model assuming the firm operates as a monopolist, and calculate the resulting price, output and profit. Now suppose the same industry operates under perfect competition then reconstruct the equilibrium under this market structure and calculate changes in the price and output. Compare and evaluate the two outcomes in terms of allocative efficiency. (6+4+2)

text: Analyze the nature of the demand curve faced by a firm under monopolistic competition. Evaluate how this structure leads to excess capacity and analyze its implications. Use suitable diagrams. (2+10)

subject: Advanced Microeconomics
text: Explain the phenomenon of price rigidity in an oligopolistic market using the kinked demand curve model. Use a suitable diagram in your explanation. During Diwali 2025, two major airlines operating on the Mumbai–Delhi route - IndiGo and Air India - must independently decide whether to charge a High fare or a Low fare. If both airlines charge High fares, each earns a profit of ₹50 crore. If IndiGo charges Low fare while Air India keeps it High, then IndiGo earns ₹60 crore and Air India earns ₹20 crore. If Air India charges Low fare while IndiGo keeps it High, Air India earns ₹60 crore and IndiGo earns ₹20 crore. If both airlines charge Low fares, each earns ₹30 crore. Construct the strategic game by designing the payoff matrix representing the interaction between the two firms. Analyze the strategic choices of both firms and determine whether a dominant strategy Nash equilibrium exists. (6+2+4)

subject: Advanced Microeconomics
text: Read the following case and answer the questions that follow: Arvion Biocare Ltd., a Mumbai-based pharmaceutical manufacturer, produces a life-saving anti-malarial drug under the brand name Malarix. In the domestic Indian market, the medicine is sold at ₹200 per unit. However, Arvion exports the same drug to several African nations at

subject: Advanced Microeconomics
text: significantly lower price of ₹120 per unit. The company explains that the African market is highly competitive and extremely price-sensitive due to lower income levels and the presence of international generic manufacturers. In contrast, domestic demand in India is relatively inelastic because the drug has limited substitutes and strong brand recognition. By charging lower prices abroad, Arvion aims to expand its global market share and utilize excess production capacity. At the same time, higher domestic prices help the firm recover research and development expenses. Recently, trade authorities in one importing country have alleged that Arvion Biocare is engaging in unfair trade practices by selling below domestic prices thereby harming local pharmaceutical producers. Questions: 1. Identify the pricing strategy followed by Arvion Biocare Ltd. Give reasons based on the case facts. 2. Explain the factors that justify and enable the firm’s pricing decision. 3. Discuss two possible economic effects of this pricing strategy on the importing country. marks)
